steps: Statement 1 is justified: at every age both columns are higher in 2019 than in 1989, for example age 19 boys 163.5 to 166.5 and girls 151.9 to 155.2 (some ages dipped slightly in between, for example boys aged 15, 155.4 to 155.2 from 1989 to 1999).
Statement 2 is not justified: 13-year-old girls in 1989 are 143.2, less than 14-year-old girls in 2009 at 148.
Statement 3 is justified: 15-year-old boys in 2019 are 159, more than 16-year-old boys in 1989 at 158.9.
Statement 4 is not justified: averages say nothing about every girl; some 11-year-olds can be taller than some 13-year-olds.
Statement 5 is not justified: girls' averages are higher at ages 11 and 12 in every year, for example 2019 age 11, 138.6 against 137.
Statement 6 cannot be decided: the table stops at 19; in 2019 boys grew only 166.5 − 166 = 0.5 cm from 18 to 19.
With 1 unit = 4°C, 20°C is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 units and 43°C is 43 ÷ 4 = 10.75 units.
Draw two bars at each time, one for each day.
Day 1 runs from 16°C to 34°C, a range of 34 − 16 = 18°C, mean 188 ÷ 8 = 23.5°C.
Day 2 runs from 30°C to 43°C, a range of 43 − 30 = 13°C, mean 295 ÷ 8 = 36.875°C.
Cool nights near 16°C suggest winter, for example December or January.
Nights of 30°C or more and an afternoon of 43°C suggest peak summer, for example May or June.
